items.text: Major supermarket chains across France were hit by an unprecedented cyberattack that targeted commercial refrigeration systems. Hackers remotely took control of thermostats in hundreds of stores, and raised temperatures in fridges and freezers to as high as 50°C. The sudden heat caused thousands of tons of fresh and frozen food, including meat, dairy, and juice, to spoil completely. This resulted in millions of dollars in damages and even triggered fires at several locations. The attack exploited security vulnerabilities in outdated control software, which allowed store managers to control appliances remotely. Major retailers like Intermarché and Carrefour were heavily affected, and forced some locations to manually disconnect their refrigeration units to prevent further tampering . French authorities and national cybersecurity agencies have launched an urgent criminal investigation into the incident, and raised serious concerns about the safety and security of essential infrastructure. Difficult words: unprecedented (an illegal attempt to damage, or steal data from computer systems or networks), thermostat (a device that automatically controls temperature in an appliance or building), vulnerability (a weakness in a system or software), tamper (to change something in order to cause damage or gain an advantage). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Big supermarkets in France suffered a strange cyberattack when hackers took control of their refrigerators and freezers. The hackers remotely raised the temperatures inside the appliances, which ruined huge amounts of fresh food like meat and dairy, and even started small fires in some stores. Big retail companies were badly hit, and lost millions of euros. Experts say the hackers broke into old software, which stores use to manage their fridges from afar. Because the software was outdated , the system was not secure. Store managers turned off remote controls to keep their shops safe. French authorities are investigating the attack to find out who is responsible. They also worry that more similar attack may come in the future. Difficult words: remotely (from a distance), outdated (old, not modern), investigate (to examine a crime or problem to discover the truth). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hackers attack big supermarkets in France. They use computers to make store fridges very hot. Because of the heat , a lot of meat, milk, and food goes bad. Workers must throw it away. Some stores are even on fire. The hackers break into an old software system. This system controls the fridges. Many stores lose a lot of money. They must turn off their machines to be safe. The French government is now looking for the people who do this bad thing. People are worried. They see that computer systems can be easy to break. Difficult words: fridge (a large appliance which keeps food fresh and cold), heat (when something is hot), turn off (to stop a machine or light). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new investigation has revealed that former Chelsea FC owner Roman Abramovich used fake, backdated financial documents to hide his wealth and avoid paying taxes. The leak shows that Cyprus-based financial firms, along with major global accounting advisers, helped rewrite company records to secret away over 600 million dollars in luxury assets, including superyachts, private jets, and luxury homes. These firms also changed bank records to help the Russian oligarch avoid paying millions of dollars in local taxes on a 2 billion dollar fortune. Since Russia invaded Ukraine, Abramovich has faced heavy international sanctions over his close ties to Vladimir Putin, which forced him to move his massive superyachts to safe waters in Turkey. While legal experts argue that these fake records amount to clear tax fraud that should face criminal prosecution, Abramovich’s legal team strongly denies any wrongdoing and insists he simply followed professional financial advice. Difficult words: secret away (to hide or place something in a secret location so others cannot find or see it), oligarch (a very rich and powerful business leader who often has strong connections to political leaders), fraud (the crime of tricking people or changing information to illegally get money or power). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new investigation shows how Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich hid his great wealth to avoid paying taxes. Secret documents show that companies in Cyprus wrote fake and backdated papers for him. These papers helped hide over 600 million dollars worth of luxury items, including yachts, private planes, and expensive houses. The advisers also changed bank records, so Abramovich wouldn’t have to pay millions in taxes. Today, Abramovich faces strict sanctions in many countries because of his close relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin. He can no longer do business in Britain, and his large superyachts are now parked in Turkey. Experts say changing official financial records to avoid taxes is against the law. Abramovich denies doing anything wrong and says he only followed advice from his financial team. Difficult words: avoid (to stay away from something or prevent something bad from happening), backdate (to put an earlier date on an official document), advice (an opinion given to help someone decide what to do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Roman Abramovich is a rich man from Russia. He owns Chelsea Football Club some time ago. A new report shows that he uses fake papers to hide his money and pay less tax . Advisers help him hide big boats, planes, and expensive houses. These things cost hundreds of millions of dollars. Because he is a close friend of Russia’s president, many countries stop him from doing business there. Now, his big boats are in Turkey. Experts say that hiding money with fake papers is a crime . Abramovich says that he does nothing wrong. He only does what his advisers tell him to do. Difficult words: hide (to put something in a place where others cannot see or find it), tax (money which you must pay to the government), crime (an illegal action). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Villagers in central India are protesting against a massive government project to link two major rivers in order to help millions of local farmers. The plan aims to build a large dam and move water to areas facing severe drought; however, construction work has already caused rising waters to flood nearby villages, homes, and a local temple. Angry residents say the government is not giving them enough money or a new place to rebuild their lives. Some protesters have even taken extreme actions, like lying on fake funeral fires to show their anger. At the same time, environmental experts warn that the new dam will destroy large areas of forest and harm rare wildlife inside a famous tiger reserve. While government officials claim the project will solve long-term water shortages and bring power to the region, critics argue the scientific plans are flawed and urge leaders to protect both local communities and nature. Difficult words: rare (not common or frequent; very unusual), shortage (a situation where there is not enough of something that people need), flawed (not perfect). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In India, many villagers are protesting against a big government plan to join two rivers. The government wants to build a big dam to bring water to dry areas and help farmers grow food. But rising water from the construction is already flooding homes, farmland, and temples. Local people say the government is taking their land without giving them enough money or a new home. Some protesters say they will not leave their land. Nature experts are also worried because the project will flood a large forest and hurt tigers living in a famous reserve . Government leaders say the project is needed to solve water problems, but many locals and experts want the government to stop and fix these serious problems first. Difficult words: dam (a strong wall built across a river to stop or control the flow of water), flood (to cover a place with a large amount of water), reserve (a protected area of land kept for wild animals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in India are very angry today. The government wants to build a big dam . They want to connect two rivers. The government says that the dam will bring water to dry places and help farmers. But water is now coming into villages, homes, and farms. Many people lose their houses. They do not have enough money to build new ones. People stand in the water to protest and ask for help. Nature experts are also worried because the water will hurt trees and tigers in a big park. The government says that the project is important , but people want to stay on their land. Difficult words: dam (a strong wall across a river), dry (without rain or water), important (when people need something very much). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to data, 1.7 million to 3 million young people suffer concussions each year while playing sports. Previously, the treatment for concussions in young people was rest. However, researchers at Children’s National Hospital in Washington, D.C. suggest that rest may no longer be the best treatment for young people with concussions. Pediatric neuropsychologist Dr. Chris Vaughan said that there was a time when a diagnosis involved a couple of fingers and if the patient could stand, they could return to play. Researchers found that children who missed less school after a concussion had fewer lingering symptoms, indicating that returning to school and daily life may be therapeutic for the brain. The study suggests that parents with children who suffer concussions should push socialization , reduce school-related stress, maintain a normal sleep/wake schedule, and encourage light-to-moderate physical activity. The findings reinforce the idea that there are things that can be done to help treat concussions in children and that it is not a wait-and-see type of injury. Difficult words: lingering (lasting for a long time), socialization (the activity with others), reinforce (to strengthen or support). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hannah Parmenter, who is now 21, got a serious concussion when she was 11 while playing soccer. She still has problems from the concussion today. 1.7 million to 3 million young people get concussions every year from playing sports. Doctors used to think that rest was the best t reatment for concussions in children. But these days, researchers think that returning to school soon after a concussion might be better. Children who missed less school had fewer problems after two weeks. This means that returning to school and daily life may help the brain recover . Doctors recommend that parents with children who get concussions should help them socialize, not miss too much school, sleep well, and do light exercise. The research shows that doctors can help kids with concussions, and they should not just wait for them to get better. Difficult words: concussion (brain injury), treatment (medical care), recover (to be healthy again). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hannah Parmenter hits her head hard when she is playing soccer at age 11. She is 21 years old now. She still has problems today. Many young people hit their heads when they play sports. Rest is the best thing for people with head injuries . That is what doctors think in the past. But now, doctors say that going back to school soon might be better. Children who miss less school have fewer problems later. This means that going back to school helps the brain feel better. Doctors say that parents should help kids be with their friends, not worry about school, sleep well, and exercise a little. Doctors can help kids with head injuries. Parents should not just wait for them to feel better. Difficult words: hit (to bring the head in contact with an object), injury (when someone gets hurt). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for solving a long-standing scientific mystery regarding molecular mirror images. Many chemical molecules exist in two mirror-image forms, much like a person’s left and right hands. In nature, living things almost always use only one version, while the other form is absent or inactive. Producing just the helpful version has historically been a huge challenge for chemical manufacturing. Controlling this balance is critical for medicine because two mirror-image molecules can have vastly different effects on the human body. For instance, while one version of a drug acts as a helpful painkiller, its mirror image can be inactive or even highly dangerous, as seen in historical medical tragedies. The duo ’s discovery of unique chemical processes allows scientists to selectively produce the safe, effective version of a molecule. This breakthrough has revolutionized the pharmaceutical industry and made everyday medicines far safer and more effective. Difficult words: absent (not present or not existing in a place), duo (two people who work or perform together), revolutionize (to completely change the way something is done or made). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Nobel Prize in Chemistry was given to two scientists, Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai. They solved a big science mystery about molecules which look like mirror images. In nature, many small chemicals come in two forms, like left and right hands. Living things usually use only one form to create life, but scientists didn’t know why. This discovery is extremely important for making medicine. One mirror-image form of a drug can heal a patient, while the other form might do nothing or even cause harm. In the past, mixed drugs caused terrible health problems for many people. Thanks to these two researchers, chemical companies can now make only the good, safe version of a drug. This makes everyday medicines much safer for everyone. Difficult words: mystery (something difficult to understand or explain), heal (to become healthy again), terrible (very bad, unpleasant, or shocking). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two scientists win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. They solve a secret about molecules. Molecules are very small parts of life. Many molecules have two forms, like a left hand and a right hand. Nature only uses one form to make living things grow. This discovery helps doctors and scientists make safer medicine. Sometimes, one form of a drug can help a sick person, but the other form can be dangerous or bad. Now, scientists know how to make only the good and safe form of a drug. This discovery saves many lives and helps people stay healthy every day. Difficult words: secret (something what most people do not know about), discovery (finding or learning about something new for the first time), dangerous (not safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Jinwar is a village in the Kurdish region in northeast Syria where a group of women displaced by war and domestic violence found a safe refuge and rebuilt their lives. Jinwar means ‘women’s space’ in the Kurdish language. The village was built in 2018, and it has 30 houses hosting 20 families of women and children. Jinwar has a school, a training academy, a bakery, and fields cultivated by women. Men aren’t allowed to live in Jinwar; however, they can visit their relatives living there. Boys who live with their mothers can stay in the village until they get married. The head of the village says women and children are always the victims in conflicts like the civil war that broke out in 2011. Women in the village spend their days working and evenings singing and dancing. Many say that they have goals and ambitions, and they can live their lives without any interference from anyone or without being controlled. They become stronger and they aren’t viewed as being confined to the household and its duties anymore. Difficult words: interference (getting involved annoyingly), confine (to keep or restrict someone). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Jinwar is a village situated in the Kurdish area of northeast Syria. Women moved here because of war and domestic violence . The name Jinwar means ‘women’s space’ in the Kurdish language. The village was built in 2018, and it consists of 30 houses. 20 families live in the village, but only women and children can live there. Men are not allowed to live in Jinwar, but they can visit their female relatives . Boys can stay with their mothers until they get married. The village has a school, a training academy, a bakery, and fields where women grow crops. In 2011, the civil war began in Syria, and women and children are the most affected . The women in the village work during the day and spend their evenings singing and dancing. They finally feel that they can live happy lives without control and rules from their families. Difficult words: domestic violence (when people of one family behave badly towards each other), relative (a person who belongs to the same family), affected (influenced). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Jinwar is a village in northeast Syria. It is a safe place for women. Workers build the village in 2018. The village has 30 houses. Women and children live there together. There are 20 families. The village has a school, a training academy, and a bakery. Women grow crops in fields. No men can live in Jinwar, but they can visit their families. Boys can live with their mothers until they get married. When there is a war, women and children always suffer the most. Women in Jinwar work during the day and sing and dance at night. They have their own goals and dreams. Nobody controls them. They become stronger. They do not just do chores at home anymore. Difficult words: crop (a plant which a farmer grows), suffer (to have a hard time), chore (a job which someone must do at home). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A couple from Canada, Denise Tisor and David Blake, went to court after scamming over 100 Taylor Swift fans out of 265 thousand dollars. Tisor sold non-existent tickets for the Eras Tour in Toronto. Many parents bought them as special gifts for their kids, including a sick girl who was seeking relief from medical struggles. Victims only found out the tickets didn’t exist right before the show, and many families were left in tears outside the stadium. Both Tisor and her husband admitted they were guilty. They also confessed to spending nearly 140 thousand dollars of the stolen money on online gambling. Lawyers are asking the judge to give them house arrest instead of sending them to real prison. However, the victims are angry about this idea and think the couple should go to jail. The court will make a final choice about their punishment in December. Difficult words: scam (a clever scheme to trick people out of their money), relief (a pleasant feeling when worry, pain, or trouble stops), punishment (a penalty given to someone because they broke a rule or law). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A couple from Canada went to court after tricking more than 100 people in a big ticket scam . The woman sold fake tickets for a Taylor Swift concert in Toronto and stole 265 thousand dollars. Many parents bought these tickets as gifts for their children. Some fans found out the tickets were fake right before the show started and cried outside the building. The couple admitted they sold the tickets and said they spent almost 140,000 on online gambling. Lawyers asked the judge for house arrest instead of real prison time for both of them. Many victims are angry about this deal and want the couple to go to prison. The court will decide on their punishment in December. Difficult words: scam (a clever idea to trick people out of their money), admit (to agree that something is true or that you did something wrong), punishment (a penalty for someone who breaks a rule or law). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A woman and her husband in Canada steal money from more than 100 people. They sell fake tickets for a big Taylor Swift concert in Toronto. They take 265,000 dollars. Many parents buy the tickets for their children. People find out that the tickets are fake just before the concert. They are very sad. The couple says sorry. They use the money to gamble online. Lawyers want the couple to stay at home for punishment instead of going to prison. Many people with the fake tickets are angry. They want them in prison. In December, we will know what will happen with them. Difficult words: husband (a married man), gamble (to risk money on a game or race), punishment (what happens to you when you break a rule). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Malaysia is making a strong push to turn durian from a simple roadside snack into a luxury global product. The country is targeting China, the world’s biggest durian market. Companies in Kuala Lumpur are launching durian-themed items like cakes and ice cream, while a new 2-million-dollar experience centre introduces tourists to Malaysian durian culture. Unlike Thailand, which harvests durians early and controls 81% of China’s market, Malaysia lets its fruit naturally ripen and fall from the tree. This natural method creates superior flavor, but the short shelf life of two to three days creates a difficult race against time. Since Malaysia only began exporting fresh durians to China in 2024, its export value quadrupled in early 2026. However, sellers note that durian is a luxury item rather than a necessity, which makes sales very sensitive to economic conditions. Thanks to social media, interest in Malaysian durian varieties is growing rapidly among Chinese consumers. Difficult words: ripen (to become fully grown and ready to eat), superior (better in quality, rank, or value than other things), shelf life (how long food or products stay fresh and safe to eat on a store shelf). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Malaysia is working hard to promote its durian fruit to the world, especially to buyers in China. In Kuala Lumpur, businesses are creating new durian products like ice cream and cakes, and opening special centers for tourists. China imports a lot of durian, but most of it currently comes from Thailand. Malaysian durians are special because farmers let them ripen on the tree and fall naturally. This gives a great taste, but the fruit spoils in just two or three days, which makes transport difficult. Malaysia started sending fresh durians to China in 2024, and sales grew quickly in 2026. Sellers say durian is a luxury food, so people buy it mainly when the economy is good. Social media is now helping more Chinese tourists discover and try Malaysian durians. Difficult words: promote (to make people to buy, use, or support something), currently (right now), ripen (to become fully grown and ready to eat). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Malaysia wants to sell more durian fruit to other countries, especially China. China buys a lot of durians, but most come from Thailand. In Malaysia, people are making durian ice cream, cakes, and special shops for tourists. Malaysian durians fall naturally from the tree when they are ready. They taste very good, but they go bad in two or three days. Selling fresh durians to China starts in 2024. They quickly become popular. People say that durian is a special food, not everyday food. Today, many people see durians on social media and travel to try this special fruit. Difficult words: durian (a large tropical fruit with a strong smell), especially (more than usual, more than other things), naturally (without people’s help). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lithuania’s parliament has taken a historic step to change its constitution, which aims to remove a long-standing ban on hosting foreign nuclear weapons on its soil. Originally introduced after the fall of the Soviet Union to speed up the departure of Russian troops, the constitutional ban is now seen as outdated given current security threats. Bordered by Russia’s Kaliningrad region and Russian ally Belarus, both believed to host nuclear warheads, Lithuania seeks to strengthen its position within NATO. The political move comes as US President Donald Trump expressed openness to establishing a permanent US military base in the country, an idea strongly welcomed by Lithuania’s prime minister to deter potential Russian aggression. However, Russia reacted with severe threats and warned it will target nuclear weapons at Lithuania if warheads are deployed there. Experts view Lithuania’s vote as a strong political signal that the nation is determined to defend its sovereignty and secure NATO corridors like the Suwalki Gap. Difficult words: outdated (old-fashioned and no longer useful or suitable for the current time), deter (to discourage or prevent someone from doing something by making them fear the consequences), sovereignty (the full power and right of a country to govern itself without outside control). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The parliament of Lithuania voted to start changing its constitution so it can allow nuclear weapons on its land in the future. Lithuania made a law against nuclear weapons years ago when the Soviet Union ended. But today, leaders feel unsafe because Lithuania shares borders with Belarus and Kaliningrad, where Russia keeps nuclear weapons. US President Donald Trump recently said he might build a permanent American military base in Lithuania, which Lithuanian leaders fully support to stay safe. In response, Russia threatened to aim its nuclear weapons at Lithuania if foreign warheads arrive. Lithuanian leaders say they are ready to protect their country and stay strong with their NATO allies. Difficult words: constitution (the basic laws of a country), permanent (something what lasts for a long time), aim (to point a weapon at a specific target). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lithuania votes today to change its laws about nuclear weapons. Long ago, Lithuania says no to nuclear weapons in the country. Now, leaders want to change the law to make the country safer. Lithuania is near Russia and Belarus. Both countries have big weapons. US President Donald Trump says that the US may build a military base in Lithuania. Local leaders like this idea. But Russia is angry. Leaders make threats against Lithuania. Leaders in Lithuania want to stay strong and work closely with their friends to stay safe. Difficult words: law (an official rule), military base (a place where soldiers live and train), threat (when you say that you will hurt someone or cause problems for them if they do or do not do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Indonesia’s top court has thrown out a case against Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka over his high school credentials . Gibran is the oldest son of former President Joko Widodo. Critics claimed his high school diploma didn’t meet national requirements for office and wanted to remove him. Under Indonesian election laws, anyone running for vice president must finish high school or must hold a qualification equivalent to it. All nine judges dismissed the case for legal reasons. They said petitioners didn’t have the right to do so because they were not candidates in the 2024 election. Also, since Gibran has already been sworn in, it is too late to change the election results. However, the judges pointed out that nobody actually showed a graduation certificate to prove his foreign credentials match local standards. So while Gibran remains in power, this issue might cause more trouble for him later on. Difficult words: credentials (official documents or achievements that prove your skills, background, or education), equivalent (having the same value, amount, or importance as something else), swear (to make a serious formal promise to tell the truth or perform official duties). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The top court in Indonesia dismissed a legal case against Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka. Some people tried to remove him from office and said his school diploma from another country was not high enough for a vice president. Under Indonesian law, leaders must finish high school or a school equal to it. All nine judges on the court rejected the case for technical legal reasons. They said the people who brought the case were not allowed to do it because they didn’t run in the 2024 election. The judges also said Gibran is already officially in office. The court noted that nobody showed anything to prove his foreign diploma was valid . For now, Gibran stays in his position, but more legal problems may happen in the future. Difficult words: dismiss (to throw out or reject a court case, idea, or statement), diploma (an official document about your studies), equal (the same in size, value, or quality), valid (officially accepted). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A top court in Indonesia decides about the vice president , Gibran. Some people want him to leave his job. They say that he does not have the right school paper from a foreign school. In Indonesia, top leaders must finish high school. All judges on the court stop the case . They say that the people who start the case are not part of the 2024 election. Also, Gibran is already in his job. But the judges also say that no one shows a real school paper on the court day. Gibran keeps his job as vice president for now. It is possible that he may have more problems with his papers later. Difficult words: vice president (the politician below the president), foreign (from another country), case (a legal problem in a court). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Reports of a lab worker dying from suspected pneumonic plague at a research institute in Irkutsk, Siberia, have raised fresh pandemic fears across Russia and Europe. Russian health authorities claim the cause of death is still unconfirmed and insist no special emergency measures have been introduced. However, residents remain divided; while some trust official reports and point out that contacts were quickly isolated, others suspect a laboratory leak or a government cover-up . International experts note that while the plague sounds like a terrifying medieval disease, hundreds of cases occur naturally each year in places like Madagascar and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Virologists emphasize that because the incident happened inside a laboratory, heightened public worry is understandable, especially after the COVID-19 pandemic. Still, global health organizations suggest that if no secondary cases appear in the coming days, the situation is likely a small, contained incident rather than a widespread health threat. Difficult words: cover-up (an attempt to hide a mistake, crime, or dangerous truth from the public), medieval (connected to the period of European history between 500 and 1500 AD), secondary (happening as a result of a main or first event), contained (kept within fixed limits and prevented from spreading). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People in the Siberian city of Irkutsk are worried after a laboratory worker died from a suspected plague infection. Russian authorities say the cause of death is not confirmed yet and there is no big danger. Some local people believe the government, while others fear the virus escaped from the research lab. Health experts explain that plague cases happen every year in places like Africa, but a lab incident naturally frightens people after the COVID-19 pandemic. International leaders and the EU are trying to get clear information from the Russian government. Experts say that if no other people get sick in the next few days, this situation is likely a small, isolated event and not a dangerous new pandemic. Difficult words: suspected (what people believe to be true but there is no evidence for it yet), plague (a serious infection which kills many people), isolated (when something happens only once or is separated from everything else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A lab worker in Siberia dies. People are scared that it is the plague . Russian leaders say that they are not sure. They do not know why the worker dies. They tell people to stay calm. Some people in the city believe the news. Others worry because it happens in a lab. Many people remember the COVID-19 pandemic. Experts say that the plague happens every year in places like Africa. People should not panic . Leaders and the EU want to know what really happens. Experts say that if no other people get sick soon, everything will be fine and safe. Difficult words: lab (a room where scientists do tests and experiments), plague (a serious infection which kills many people), panic (a strong feeling when you worry very much). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hello students, We have a website for you. Its name is www.speakinlevels.com . You can use filters to search for people at your level, by country, or by gender (female or male) and speak with them. You can also easily write to people via a form and you will be informed about new people who are ready to talk with you. There are also conversation topics and tips on how to start communication with new people. We hope that you will find a lot of new friends for daily conversation in English and that this project will help you improve your English speaking skills! Have a nice day, News in Levels team

Hello students, We have a website for you. Its name is www.speakinlevels.com . You can use filters to search for people at your level and speak with them. You can also search for people by country or gender (men or women). You can also use a form to write to people, and you will be informed when people are ready to talk with you. Are you afraid to talk with somebody who you don’t know? Don’t worry! There are tips and topics which can help you start talking. Have fun and speak with your new friends ! We hope that you will improve your English! Have a nice day, News in Levels team

Hello students, There is a website for you. It is www.speakinlevels.com . It is for students of English. It is for speaking. You can find people at your level of English. You can find people from different countries. You can choose to talk to men or women. Are you afraid of new people? Don’t worry! With Speak in Levels, you can start easily. There are tips on the website. These tips can help you. Speak in Levels can help your English. Have fun with it! Have a nice day, News in Levels team

Do you ever feel like the internet is getting weirder and less useful? You are not alone. More and more people worry AI is slowly killing the web by flooding it with cheap, machine-made articles. Right now, bots make up over 60% of all web traffic, and AI writes a huge chunk of new pages. It is part of the dead internet theory , the idea that real human content is vanishing . Even big tech bosses know there is a problem. Their smart AI search tools steal summaries from human writers, so people stop clicking on actual websites. That means real newsrooms lose money and go bust . Once human writers disappear, AI will start learning from its own low-quality content and create lots of mistakes and bad advice. To save the web, we need to click on original sources, check who wrote what, and support real human journalists. Difficult words: chunk (a large piece or part of something), vanish (to disappear completely and suddenly), go bust (to lose all money and be forced to close a business). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many people worry that the internet is dying because AI is creating too much text and too many images. Today, automated bots make up more than 60% of web activity, and many new websites use AI to write articles. This problem is called the dead internet theory . Tech companies know this is dangerous because AI tools copy work from real human writers. When people read quick AI summaries, they don’t click on the original websites, so human writers lose money and close their businesses. In the future, AI will train on bad AI-generated content, spread mistakes, false news, and wrong health advice. To stay safe, readers should always check who wrote an article, look at real source websites, and support human journalists. Difficult words: automated (done by machines or computers instead of people), human (about real people), AI-generated (created by AI). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Is the internet dying? Today, many computers and AI tools write texts on the web. More than half of web traffic comes from bots , not real people. AI tools take words from human writers and make short summaries . Because of this, people do not visit real websites. Real writers lose their jobs and money. When they stop making new texts, AI will start learning from bad AI texts. This will bring more mistakes in news and health tips. To help, we should check who writes a text, click on real web pages, and help real writers. Difficult words: traffic (how many people or bots visit a website), bot (a computer program which works alone), summary (a short text which gives you the main idea of a longer text). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tens of thousands of students and teachers have taken to the streets across France to protest severe under-investment in public high schools. Protesters are demanding immediate action over overcrowded classrooms, decaying 1970s buildings with leaking roofs and rats, and long-term teacher shortages caused by years of budget cuts. The movement, which started in deprived Parisian suburbs, has quickly turned into a nationwide crisis. However, the protests have grown increasingly violent over the past three weeks, and resulted in thousands of arrests, damaged schools, and injuries on both sides, including a 15-year-old student who lost his hand to a police grenade. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu strongly condemned the rioting and insisted that destroying schools doesn’t solve funding problems. While police have used tear gas to disperse crowds, demonstrators accuse authorities of using heavy-handed tactics. With a presidential election just six months away, these widespread demonstrations highlight deep social political divisions across the country. Difficult words: under-investment (providing less money or funding than is necessary for something to work properly), deprived (suffering from a lack of necessary resources, money, and good living conditions), heavy-handed (using too much force or authority to control a situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Thousands of students and teachers are protesting across France because public high schools are in terrible condition. Classrooms are overcrowded, buildings are falling apart with leaks and rats, and there are not enough substitute teachers when staff are sick. The protests began near Paris and spread to many cities. Unfortunately, some protests became very violent . Protesters set fire to bins and damaged school buildings, while riot police used tear gas and grenades to clear the streets. Police arrested thousands of people. The French Prime Minister said that violence will not fix the school system. With an important presidential election coming in six months, these angry protests show that the country is divided over public education and government spending. Difficult words: substitute teacher (a teacher who takes over a class when the regular teacher is sick or away), violent (when someone uses force to hurt people or break things), divided (split into different groups with different ideas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of students and teachers in France are protesting today. They are angry because high school buildings are old, dirty , and broken. Many classes are full, and there are not enough teachers. The protests start near Paris and are now everywhere in the country. Sadly, some protests become violent . People burn bins and break school doors. Police must stop them. Thousands of people go to prison, and some people get hurt. Leaders say that these protests will not help schools. France is voting for a new president in six months. It is a big problem for many people. They are worried about their schools. Difficult words: dirty (not clean), violent (when someone uses force to hurt people or break things), vote (when people choose a new leader or someone for an important job). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For 25 years, Disney’s Animal Kingdom has been leading worldwide conservation efforts to increase the populations of threatened animals and restore their habitats. With one of the world’s largest veterinarian hospitals, the park cares for all animal species, not just the big charismatic ones. The Animal Nutrition Center staff oversees 1,500 different diets and delivers 10,000 pounds of food to animals every day. The Disney Conservation Fund has directed 120 million dollars to help save wildlife. The team designs wildlife and animal habitats in the parks, such as Wishing Star Lake, created for struggling bird populations in Shanghai Disney Resort. The hope is that the threatened and endangered butterflies, including the monarch, will thrive in pollinator gardens across all the Disney properties. On Earth Day, the conservation experts encourage everyone to grow a pollinator garden to help care for their local animal kingdom. Difficult words: conservation (protecting earth’s resources for future generations), charismatic (likable and naturally drawing attention), pollinator garden (a garden designed to grow specific nectar and pollen-producing plants). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Disney’s Animal Kingdom worked for 25 years to increase the population of threatened animals such as lions, giraffes, and rhinos. They have a large animal hospital which takes care of all animals, not just the popular ones. The staff manages 1,500 diets and feeds 4,500 kilograms of food to animals every day. Disney also supports wildlife conservation with 120 million dollars. They partnered with researchers to use bees to keep elephants away from African farms. Now they want to help threatened butterflies, like the monarch, by creating pollinator gardens . On Earth Day, conservation experts asked people to grow their own pollinator gardens which help their local animal kingdom. Even you can plant milkweed and create your own pollinator garden. Difficult words: threatened (someone or something in danger), wildlife conservation (protecting plants and animals and their homes), pollinator garden (a special garden in which people grow plants that produce food for insects and other small animals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Disney loves animals and wants to help them. They have a big hospital for animals. The staff prepares 1,500 different diets. They give the animals 4,500 kilograms of food every day. They want to save threatened animals , like lions, giraffes, and rhinos, and help them live in their homes. Disney gives lots of money to protect animals. They use bees to keep elephants away from farms. They want to help butterflies by planting milkweed in gardens. Difficult words: staff (people who work in one company), threatened animal (an animal which is in danger and may not exist anymore), milkweed (a plant which has white milky sap, and butterflies like it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

As offshore wind energy rapidly expands across Europe, scientists are using thermal cameras and AI to study the impact of wind turbines on migrating birds. Millions of birds cross the North Sea every year; however, it is difficult to measure collision risks at sea due to dark night conditions and remote locations. In a year-long pilot study at a Dutch wind farm, researchers placed sixteen thermal cameras on a turbine to monitor bird activity day and night. Out of millions of bird movements recorded over two migration seasons, the team identified only two confirmed collisions. Other studies used radar technology and similarly showed that over 99.8% of migrating birds successfully avoid turbine blades . While these initial findings suggest that offshore wind farms pose a lower threat than previously feared, conservationists emphasize that careful site selection, smart technology, and protective measures remain important to protect endangered seabird populations during the clean energy transition. Difficult words: turbine (a machine with blades that are turned by water, wind, or steam to produce power), blade (a wide, flat arm on a propeller or wind turbine that spins in the air), conservationist (a person who works to protect animals, plants, and natural environments). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

European countries are building many new wind turbines in the sea to create clean energy, and scientists want to know if these big turbines are dangerous for migrating birds. Every year, millions of birds fly across the North Sea, but checking for accidents at sea is difficult, especially at night. To solve this problem, researchers installed sixteen special thermal cameras and AI on a sea turbine. During a one-year test, the cameras recorded millions of bird flights, but they only found two confirmed bird collisions. Other recent studies also show that almost all birds learn to fly around the turbines safely. Even though these results are good news, nature experts say we must keep using technology and careful planning to protect wild birds and their habitats . Difficult words: wind turbine (a tall structure which turns wind power into electricity), thermal camera (a special which records heat), habitat (the natural home or environment of an animal or plant species). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Countries in Europe build big wind turbines in the sea for clean energy from wind. But millions of birds fly over the sea every year. People want to keep them safe. Scientists put sixteen thermal cameras on a turbine to watch birds during the day and night. In one year, millions of birds fly near the turbine. Only two birds hit it. Other studies also show that almost all birds fly around the turbines safely. Experts say that these results are good news. But we must still help the birds and keep them safe. Difficult words: wind turbine (a tall structure which turns wind power into electricity), thermal camera (a special which records heat), result (the information which you get at the end of a test or study). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the world of luxury fashion, India plays a significant, but often hidden, role in the production process. Despite the industry’s focus on high quality, exclusivity , and European craftsmanship, many luxury fashion houses rely on India for skilled labor and embroidery work. This connection has been concealed for years to maintain a certain image and avoid concerns about working conditions. While Western luxury brands proudly display ‘Made in France’ or ‘Made in Italy’ labels, much of the intricate embroidery and labor-intensive work is actually done in India. This lack of transparency has raised questions about the ethics of the fashion industry. One example is a jacket that retails for 43,000 Euros and underwent over 2,000 hours of embroidery work in India; however, it received less than 100 hours of finishing touches in Europe, despite bearing a ‘Made in France’ label. Despite these practices, some luxury brands are beginning to acknowledge their Indian suppliers and promote India’s artisanal legacy. However, it remains a complex issue in an industry built on exploitation and secrecy. Difficult words: exclusivity (the quality of being limited to rich people), embroidery (decorating fabric or other materials with needle and thread, often creating intricate designs), artisanal (made traditionally). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the luxury fashion industry, India has an important part in the production. Even though luxury fashion brands emphasize quality and European skills, they often rely on India for embroidery work and other skills. Companies didn’t speak about this because people worried about working conditions in India’s factories. For example, a jacket which costs 43,000 Euros had over 2,000 hours of embroidery work done in India but it only received less than 100 hours of finishing touches in Europe. But there was the ‘Made in France’ label on it. Some luxury brands are starting to speak about India’s skills more. But the problem with working conditions in factories is still here. Difficult words: emphasize (to make something sound or seem more important than other things), embroidery (creating designs on fabric), finishing touch (a final detail or action which completes a piece of work). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In luxury fashion, India helps European fashion houses make clothes. India is good at making clothes. But companies do not speak much about the situation in Indian factories. Children often work there. Workers get only a little money. Big brands say ‘Made in France’ or ‘Made in Italy’ on clothes. But they really make them in India. This is not fair and transparent . One special jacket costs 43,000 Euros. India does 2,000 hours of work on it. Europe does only 100 hours. But the label says ‘Made in France’ which is not really true. Some brands are starting to say that they use India, but it is not easy in the fashion world. Difficult words: luxury (of good quality and expensive), brand (a type of product), transparent (clear). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A botched execution in Tennessee has left 50-year-old death row prisoner Christa Pike alive in hospital after surviving two lethal injections. Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for a brutal murder, was set to become the first woman executed in the state in over 200 years. However, witnesses reported seeing her continue breathing and snoring long after the pentobarbital injections were administered. Following an emergency court motion, prison officials rushed her to hospital to receive life-saving care. The horrific incident sparked immediate international outrage and prompted UN human rights officials to call the failed execution cruel and abhorrent . In response, Tennessee Governor Bill Lee launched a comprehensive investigation into the procedure and issued a temporary hold on all remaining executions scheduled for this year. The controversy has reopened major public debates across the United States regarding capital punishment and the reliability of lethal execution drugs. Difficult words: botched (done very poorly or carelessly), lethal (deadly), pentobarbital (a strong sedative drug used in medical treatments and lethal injections), abhorrent (disgusting or shocking). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A death row prisoner in Tennessee named Christa Pike is in the hospital after a failed execution attempt. Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for murder and was supposed to be the first woman executed in the state in over 200 years. During the execution, doctors gave her two lethal injections, but witnesses said she was still breathing and snoring. Her lawyers quickly stopped the process, and emergency teams rushed her to a local hospital. Following the terrible event, the governor of Tennessee stopped all executions in the state to start a full investigation. Human rights leaders from the United Nations called the failed attempt extremely cruel . This scary situation has created huge public concern across the United States about the safety and fairness of death penalty laws. Difficult words: death row (a special section of a prison for people who wait for execution), execution (the legal ending of someone’s life), lethal (deadly), cruel (when someone or something causes pain or suffering to others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A woman named Christa Pike is in the hospital. She goes to prison in 1996 for a murder. She gets the death penalty . Officials use two injections to end her life. But after that, she is still breathing and alive. Her lawyers stop the process. Doctors take her to the hospital. The leader of Tennessee stops other executions for now. Nobody knows what goes wrong. Leaders at the United Nations say that this failed event is very cruel and terrible. Many people in America are now asking big questions about death rules and safety. Difficult words: death penalty (the legal ending of the life of a person who does something very bad), fail (to not manage to do what you plan or want), cruel (when something or someone hurts others very much). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Younger generations are finding it harder than ever to reach classic adult milestones like buying a home or starting a family. Statistics show over 70% of Gen Z have delayed these major life goals due to sky-high house prices, high rent, and stagnant wages. In places like the UK, buying a property now costs up to twelve times the average salary, which makes home ownership feel like a distant dream. On top of that, social media constantly exposes young people to unrealistic standards of wealth, creates unnecessary pressure, and leads to poor financial decisions. Economic experts point out that Gen Z is projected to be less wealthy than their parents due to high interest rates and inflation. However, rather than giving up, young people are adapting, learning about personal finance, and taking to activism or public protests to demand real political change for their future. Difficult words: milestone (an important event or stage in life or development), stagnant (not growing, changing, or developing over time), projected (expected or estimated to happen or be a certain level in the future). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Young adults in Gen Z are struggling to reach traditional life goals like buying a house, getting married, or having children. High house prices, expensive rent, and low salaries mean that young people delay these milestones . In many countries, buying a home now costs up to ten times an average yearly salary. Social media makes things worse because young people compare themselves to online images of rich people, which causes stress and bad financial choices. Experts say this generation may be less rich than their parents because of inflation and high living costs. Instead of giving up, many young people are learning how to manage their money better. Many are also joining political protests to fight for lower costs, fair treatment, and a better future for everyone. Difficult words: milestone (an important event or stage in life), average (normal), inflation (when prices are rising over time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many young people today cannot reach important life goals easily. Buying a house or starting a family costs too much money. House prices and rent are very high. Job pay stays low. Social media also shows rich people who enjoy life. Young adults feel sad and confused about money. Experts say that young people today have less money than their parents. Young people are learning how to use their money better. They ask for help. Many young people are also protesting to ask politicians for fair prices, better jobs, and a good future. Difficult words: goal (something what you want to have or do in the future), rent (money which you pay to live in someone’s house or apartment), confused (when you cannot think clearly or understand something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
